piece.name: The LA Rail
piece.title: The LA Rail
piece.notes: Classic 4-minute pop song, a little prog / a little yacht rock -- Supertramp lane (Logical Song / Take the Long Way Home territory: quartal-adjacent extended chords at density='full', laid-back light-swing pocket, sax-like countermelody). Structure: intro, verse, chorus, verse, chorus, transition (real breakdown -- learned from Cakewalk Strut not to stay 'too alive' the whole way through), bridge (borrowed bVII for a modal-mixture lift + second_melody carrying a genuine polymeter drift as the 'prog' touch), final chorus modulated up a whole step G->A (uses the sec_key/sec_mode fix made today -- confirmed counterpoint and second_melody now actually follow a section-level key override instead of silently staying in the piece's original key), outro. swing=0.15 throughout on purpose (unlike the cakewalk/ragtime rule of swing=0.0 -- yacht rock's pocket, e.g. Steely Dan/Doobie Brothers, genuinely does want a light shuffle, a different genre calling for a different informed choice, not the same rule applied blindly). Counterpoint (one voice, below, sax/horn-like) present only in choruses/bridge/final chorus, absent in verses -- enters with the hook the way Xanadu's counterpoint did.

sections.name: intro
sections.notes: Short vamp, establishes the vi-IV-I-V loop before the verse states it properly.

sections.name: verse_1
sections.notes: Verse 1 -- laid back, no counterpoint yet, leaves room for the vocal/lyric. 'I'm gonna ride my daily destination, the LA Rail' territory.

sections.name: chorus_1
sections.notes: Chorus -- tonic-anchored (I, not vi), higher energy, counterpoint enters as a sax/horn-like line under the hook. syncopated groove for pop lift, still 0.15 swing underneath.

sections.name: verse_2
sections.notes: Verse 2, compressed to 12 bars for pacing -- ends on IV rather than resolving to V, leaning into chorus 2. 'This might be droll... tomorrow's dreams' territory.

sections.name: transition
sections.notes: The actual breakdown -- single held vi chord, sparse, high rest_probability, no counterpoint, no groove. Learned this lesson directly from Cakewalk Strut: a real gap here earns the bridge instead of just continuing at chorus density. This is the quiet before the bridge steps outside the song's narrative.

sections.name: bridge
sections.notes: Bridge -- steps outside the verse/chorus narrative (Star Wars / rock-and-roll-reborn-every-ten-years territory). Borrowed bVII (F major, mixolydian lift) for the 'prog' color. second_melody carries the actual polymeter payoff from today's engine work: a bell-like hit every 3 beats against the 4-beat bar, genuinely drifting through all 16 bars rather than a fixed accent -- the one place in the song the polymeter bones actually get used, not just tested. Walking bass, same 'genuinely developmental' role it played in Riff Cycle's bridge.

sections.name: final_chorus
sections.notes: Final chorus, modulated up a whole step (G->A) via section-level key override -- the 'one modulation move that reliably works' per the songwriting craft notes. This is the actual reason today's sec_key/sec_mode fix mattered: without it, counterpoint here would have silently stayed in G while melody/harmony/bass correctly moved to A.

sections.name: outro
sections.notes: Resolves in the modulated key -- ends up, doesn't come back down. Fade/decay to close.
